newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Two human rights workers slain in Colombian "atrocity".
newsitem.headline: Two human rights workers slain in Colombian "atrocity".

text.p: A suspected right-wing death squad broke into a Bogota apartment early on Monday and killed two human rights workers and a relative, police said.

A 1-year-old child escaped by hiding in a closet. Police later found the baby boy sitting between the bullet-riddled bodies of his parents, Mario and Elsa Calderon, and grandfather Carlos Alvarado. Alvarado's wife suffered multiple bullet wounds but survived.
The Calderons were university professors and also worked with a Bogota-based human rights organisation known as the Centre for Research and Popular Education CINEP.
"We don't know what the motives for the attack were. It seems it was carried out by a paramilitary group," said Roman Catholic priest Father Fernan Gonzalez, CINEP deputy director.
"Police found the child in the middle of the bodies. He had hidden in closet," he added.

Bogota police chief Gen. Teodoro Campo said five men armed with machine guns broke into the apartment in a middle-class district. They posed as members of the Chief Prosecutor's Department and said they had come to search the building.
Presidential Human Rights spokesman Carlos Vicente de Roux called for a thorough investigation.

"The way in which these people were murdered shows levels of aggression and atrocity which, if not combatted, will open the way to a wave of savagery against recognised promoters of human rights," De Roux said in a statement.
In another attack early on Monday in northern Colombia, a paramilitary gang raided a farm and killed eight peasants for allegedly collaborating with leftist guerrillas, a police spokesman said.

Over the weekend, suspected members of Uraba ACCU, the country's most-feared paramilitary squad, dragged three men from a bus, shot them to death and disfigured their corpses with a highly corrosive acid in northwest Antioquia province, Bogota's El Tiempo newspaper reported.
Right-wing death squads are locked in a bitter fight for territorial and political control over much of northern Colombia.
